rationale: Acoustics favored octanoic acid in the 16-person crossover. The soybean-oil phase had small decreases from baseline and blinded vowel and sentence ratings pointed in opposite directions. Parkinson disease was excluded. An oil-free comparison and refining grade are absent.

The registered 400-m gain was 0.089 m/s smaller with the curcumin formulation. Both arms gained speed and an exploratory Welch 95% CI crosses zero (−0.188 to +0.010 m/s). Grip changed in the opposite direction. The 17-person trial supplies competing walking context, with too little precision and outcome fit for a transferred bradykinesia direction.

DHA shortened working-memory response time versus high-oleic sunflower oil, but working-memory accuracy, attention and processing speed intervals span zero. The oil arm did not show an overall slowing from baseline. No oil-free arm, pressing grade or Parkinson population was reported.

In 9 active and 8 control participants, pain changed from 0.97 to 0.20 and from 1.30 to 1.60 on a 0–10 scale, an unadjusted descriptive contrast of −1.07 points. A change variance or between-group analysis is absent. Low baseline pain and the formulation and population differences limit culinary Parkinson inference.
